title: Browsers: which settings do you need to enforce?
short: Manage Edge and Chrome centrally, force every update to apply within 72 hours and allow sign-in only with work accounts.
answer: This month, put Edge and Chrome under central management, force every update to apply within 72 hours and allow browser sign-in only with work accounts. Judge every other browser setting by whether it keeps stolen sessions, unmanaged devices or unapproved AI tools away from company data.
audience: IT and security teams managing Windows and Mac computers, especially on Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Manage Edge and Chrome from one place.
items.text: Use Intune, Group Policy or the Edge management service for Edge[^edgemgmt], and Chrome Enterprise Core, at no additional cost, or Group Policy for Chrome[^cecore]. Block other browsers with application control, as the endpoints and email sheet describes.

items.title: Force updates to apply within 72 hours.
items.text: Updates apply only after a relaunch. Set RelaunchNotification to Required and RelaunchNotificationPeriod to 259200000 ms, the patching sheet's 72 hours. With RelaunchFastIfOutdated at 7, a browser more than a week out of date gets 2 hours[^chromepol].

items.title: Allow sign-in only with work accounts.
items.text: Set RestrictSigninToPattern to your domains in Edge and Chrome. Without Google Workspace, set Chrome's BrowserSignin to Disable[^chromepol]. This keeps work data out of personal sync accounts, as the NCSC suggests[^ncscbrowser].

items.title: Make malware and phishing warnings final.
items.text: Enable SmartScreen in Edge and block overrides with PreventSmartScreenPromptOverride and its ForFiles twin, which need domain-joined or MDM-enrolled devices[^edgesmart]. In Chrome, set SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel and DisableSafeBrowsingProceedAnyway. In both, set DownloadRestrictions to 4 to block known malicious downloads[^chromepol][^edgedl].

items.title: Let only managed devices reach company data.
items.text: Require a compliant device in Conditional Access. For personal Windows PCs, require an app protection policy: it admits Edge and blocks other browsers from Microsoft 365[^mamwin].

blocks.title: Set up the browser baseline in this order

items.title: Find every browser and extension.
items.text: Chrome Enterprise Core reports each browser's version, extensions and policies[^cecore]. Find other browsers, including AI browsers, in your device inventory.

items.title: Start from Microsoft's baseline.
items.text: Assign Intune's Edge security baseline, version 139 from April 2026[^intunebase], and match it in Chrome. Use Extended Stable, which moves every 8 weeks, only where testing needs it[^edgerelease].

items.title: Connect Chrome to Entra ID.
items.text: On Windows, set CloudAPAuthEnabled to 1. Chrome then signs users in to Microsoft sites with their Windows work account[^chromepol] and can pass device checks in Conditional Access[^cacond].

items.title: Turn off developer tools for most staff.
items.text: Set DeveloperToolsAvailability to 2; the NCSC notes the console can aid social engineering[^ncscbrowser]. Exempt developers by group, or allow internal sites with DeveloperToolsAvailabilityAllowlist[^chromepol].

items.title: Then allowlist extensions.
items.text: Follow the endpoints and email sheet, and review AI extensions first. Microsoft found one malicious extension campaign with over 900,000 installs that harvested AI chat histories and prompts[^mddr].

blocks.title: Stolen session cookies: what each defense covers
items: **Software alone can't stop cookie theft.** Google says no software-only method reliably stops it[^gdbsc]; infostealers increasingly take session tokens[^mddr].

**App-bound encryption (Windows, version 127+).** It forces malware to gain system rights or inject into the browser, so it helps most where users can't run downloads as admin[^abe]. Keep ApplicationBoundEncryptionEnabled on[^edgeabe].
**Remote debugging.** Attackers turned to it to pull cookies, so Chrome 136 blocked it on the default profile[^remotedebug]. Set RemoteDebuggingAllowed to false outside developer groups[^chromepol].

**Device Bound Session Credentials.** On by default for Google Workspace accounts in Chrome 146+ on Windows with a TPM; require it per app with context-aware access[^dbscws]. Other sites must adopt it themselves[^gdbsc].

**Entra token protection in browsers.** A preview covers the Azure portal and Entra and Intune admin centers in Edge or Chrome with Microsoft's Single Sign On extension; it blocks other web apps on Azure Resource Manager[^tpweb]. Native apps: see the passkeys and MFA sheet.

blocks.title: Profiles, sync and passwords
items: **Separate work and personal.** Edge for Business gives each its own window, cache and storage and shares no passwords between them; the personal window still gets your security and update policies[^efb]. On Google Workspace, set Chrome's ProfileSeparationSettings to Enforced[^chromepol].
**Limit what syncs.** Exclude types such as passwords with SyncTypesListDisabled[^chromepol]. The BSI's federal standard requires turning off cloud sync of credentials, cookies and history[^bsimst].

**Keep passwords in one place.** The BSI advises external password managers because built-in ones usually fall short[^bsimst]; the NCSC accepts built-in ones[^ncscbrowser]. Give staff a business password manager with SSO, shared vaults and offboarding, then set PasswordManagerEnabled to false. Saved passwords keep working[^chromepol], so have staff move them.

blocks.title: AI features and AI browsers
items: **Assume they are in use.** Microsoft saw AI browsers in daily use at over 40% of organizations in its data[^mddr]. For agent risks, see the agentic AI and AI input security sheets.

**Copilot in Edge.** EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext decides whether Copilot reads pages and history in work profiles; unset, it's off in the EU but users can turn it on[^edgecopilot]. Its browsing agent is a preview closed to EEA tenants[^bwc].

**Gemini in Chrome.** Turn it off with GeminiSettings. Its auto browse agent is off by default for managed users and follows GeminiActOnWebSettings. Gemini in Chrome isn't offered in the EU yet[^gic].
**Other AI browsers.** Block them with application control until you've checked which of your policies they honor.

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **Major releases every two weeks.** Edge 152 on 27 August and Chrome 153 on 8 September moved Stable to a two-week cycle; Extended Stable keeps eight weeks[^edgerelease][^chrome2w].
**Session binding shipped.** DBSC became publicly available in Chrome 146 on Windows in April[^gdbsc]. Entra token protection gained a browser preview for Azure admin portals[^tpweb].
**Browser agents came switched off.** Chrome's auto browse and Edge's browsing with Copilot stay off until an admin allows them[^gic][^bwc].

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **A separate enterprise browser first.** Edge management and Chrome Enterprise Core already handle policies and extensions[^edgemgmt][^cecore]. Buy Chrome Enterprise Premium only for gaps such as DLP or context-aware access[^cepricing].
**Disabling JavaScript or password autofill.** The NCSC says using the web reliably and securely is very difficult without them[^ncscbrowser].

**Copying the BSI's federal standard line by line.** Written for federal networks with a central blocklist, it says to turn off protection that calls external services[^bsimst]. You'd lose SmartScreen and Safe Browsing.

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Counting a downloaded update as installed.** Without RelaunchNotification, only a subtle menu change asks for the relaunch[^chromepol].

**Turning off app-bound encryption for roaming profiles.** It doesn't work where profiles roam[^abe], but disabling it lets other apps retrieve the browser's keys[^edgeabe]. Fix the roaming setup instead.
**Setting one policy in two consoles.** Group Policy and MDM override the Edge management service[^edgemgmt], so cloud settings can silently lose.
**Resetting only the password after an infostealer.** Invalidate sessions in every SaaS the browser used and check what the attacker reached[^mddr].

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: Standardize on Edge, manage it in Intune and assign the Edge security baseline.
Set the relaunch deadline, sign-in restriction and SmartScreen overrides from the five things.
Block unmanaged devices, or give them SharePoint's limited web-only access[^spunm].

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Enroll Chrome in Chrome Enterprise Core with the same settings.
Require Intune app protection for Edge on personal Windows PCs.
Pilot token protection in the Azure portal for admins.

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: Enforce token protection for admins and, on Google Workspace, DBSC through context-aware access.
Add browser DLP for unmanaged devices and AI sites, as the DLP sheet describes.
Report weekly on browsers past the 72-hour deadline and extensions off the allowlist.

changes.text: First draft, based on Microsoft Learn and Chrome Enterprise policy documentation, Google's and Microsoft's 2026 posts on session binding, the BSI minimum standard for web browsers, NCSC browser guidance and the Microsoft Digital Defense Report 2026.
